pageCache.text:
Find their happy place. And see them grow.
An Outstanding, Independent, Co-educational Prep School
in Hampton, South West London. Discover it for yourself.
Headmaster’s Welcome
Visit Us
You’ll soon find that academic excellence is a given here at TPS. Thanks to our talented teachers, small class sizes and innovative approaches which will intellectually stretch your son or daughter. And equip them with the soft skills vital for the future.
Academic
ISI Inspection Report 2025
But we believe learning is about so much more. Our personalised pastoral care, close-knit community, warm atmosphere and inclusive culture enable everyone to excel. Confident, capable and kind children are the result.
Wellbeing
This perfect balance of smiles and success will enable your child to reach the senior school destination that’s right for them, too.
Beyond TPS
Before all that, TPS will be their happy place. As you may already have experienced, there’s an intangible sense of joy and belonging once you arrive at our school gates in TW12…
Visit Us
We are truly delighted that TPS has met all the required standards, reflecting our commitment to provide high-quality education and exceptional care for our pupils.
For more information please read the report below
ISI Inspection Report 2025
Where next?
It was an absolute pleasure to welcome local chess players to the Hampton Junior Chess Congress on Saturday here at TPS on behalf of the Richmond Junior Chess Club. This was a qualifying tournament for the London Junior Chess Championships. With over 60 competitors from the local area playing in 3 age groups to win places to compete in the London finals. Well done to everyone who took part. @richmond_junior_chess_club #chesschampionships #LJCCQualifier
On Monday Year 1 were delighted to welcome Tortie the tortoise to TPS, where they found out all about the life of a tortoise – what they eat, how they prepare for hibernation and how to care for them. Tortie is getting ready to hibernate so is eating very little but was very happy to explore the Pre-Prep and say hello to Year 1 who loved getting to know her! #lifecycles #year1 🐢
Year 3 had a fantastic day at Ufton Court, stepping back in time for an exciting Egyptian-themed adventure! The children discovered what life was like in Ancient Egypt and learnt about the fascinating, and rather gory, process of mummification.The children also took part in a dramatic real-life Egyptian court, where they became judges and decided the punishments for a variety of crimes. The choices were certainly not for the faint-hearted, with punishments including the loss of a limb, being fed to the crocodiles, or paying a large fine!It was a fun, memorable and action-packed day, and the children thoroughly enjoyed bringing their Ancient Egypt learning to life.Thank you @ufton.court for a fantastic day #year3 #ancientegyptians
On Tuesday all our pupils enjoyed the awe and wonder of space travel as they took a trip around the Milky Way and beyond.🌌Star-spotting the constellations that will appear this week in the night’s sky with the legends from Ancient Greek mythology and exploring the sun, planets and moons in our solar system🌖Thank you @explorerdome for the incredible shows! 🪐 #science #solarsystem
It was wonderful to gather together as a whole school community for our annual Harvest Festival this week at St Mary’s Hampton.🌾After the long hot dry summer we were thinking about water and how precious this resource is to life on earth with House poems read by our competition winners and the Reverend Teri Ann delivering her address about the calming and healing properties of water. 💦 Our pupils delighted us with their singing directed by Mrs Harris and thank you to everyone who kindly donated items for The Hygiene Bank in Hampton.🙏💜Thank you @hamptonchurch for hosting us 🙏#harvestfestival #tpscommunity #thehygienebank

pageCache.text:
Headmaster’s Welcome
TPS Headmaster: Oliver Barrett
Thanks for your interest in our fantastic school.
I’ve been Headmaster at Twickenham Prep School since September 2020 and feel truly privileged to be part of such an amazing community. My first experience of visiting TPS was all about the vibrancy and warmth of the welcome, making a positive lasting impression on me. I simply had to be part of the next exciting chapter of the school’s development!
A good friend of mine, who happens to be a TPS parent, is convinced that there is ‘something magical about the colour purple’. And this encapsulates all the energy and fun which pervades the learning taking place here, reflecting the dedication and skill of the teachers and support staff who make every day a thrilling prospect for the children.
There is awe and wonder about lessons through our broad and challenging curriculum, excitement about trips, workshops and the extensive co-curricular programme, and a genuine sense for each child of being an important member of our caring community.
Of course, choosing the right school is a critical one for parents and carers; the decision will determine the nature of the environment in which your child is educated, and the values of the school will influence them for the rest of their lives.
The firm foundation derived from an outstanding independent school education here at TPS is increasingly important in these challenging times, when society needs its future leaders to be adaptable, creative and resilient, whilst demonstrating empathy and kindness.
TPS creates a foundation for life; both for today and the future, in a wonderful, co-educational setting. We aim to inspire a love of independent learning, seeking to ensure our pupils are ‘Calm, Courageous, Courteous and Considerate’.
Our school is all about nurturing happy and settled children with strong friendships and trusted teachers and support staff behind them. So TPS will truly be ‘their happy place’!
Please visit us soon to see for yourselves…
Oliver Barrett, Headmaster
Visit Us
We invite you to come and discover their happy place. Prospective parents are always welcome to TPS. We run regular termly open events and these are a great opportunity to see our school in action, have tours of the school, meet staff members and enjoy talks by our Headmaster, Head Boy and Head Girl.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music & Drama | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Music & Drama
Music is a vehicle of personal expression and creativity, and it plays an important part in the development of children.
Experiencing the joy of performing and creating music in groups is at the core of our Music teaching ethos. Pupils have the opportunity to learn instruments in class, ranging from keyboards to djembe drums and ukuleles as well as having 1:1 lessons with our large team of visiting music teachers on instruments such as the saxophone.
Music promotes emotional wellbeing, offering an outlet for self-expression and creativity.
It encourages collaboration, teamwork, and discipline through group performances and practice. This is a subject that all our pupils feel happy and comfortable in, enjoying the extensive resources we have at TPS.
Drama
At the heart of TPS drama is our commitment to support children’s creative and communicative growth as well as to help them discovery their sense of individuality and inner confidence.
We believe in non-judgemental and inspiring rehearsal spaces where pupils can use their imagination to help develop their vocal, physical and storytelling skills through both improvisation and scripted activities.
Working individually, in small groups or with larger casts for production work, children are encouraged to find joy in both the collaborative process as well as a feeling of accomplishment in performing in front of an audience.
We also support pupils’ understanding and appreciation of technical aspects of theatre, including sound, lighting and digital media.

Art & DT
Art and Design Technology are highly valued and exciting components of our curriculum.
Our lessons aim to stimulate pupils’ creativity and imagination, enabling them to communicate their observations, thoughts and feelings through the use of colour, form, pattern and a wide variety of materials and processes.
Our Pre-Prep pupils are introduced to art and design technology within their classrooms through a topic-based approach, inspiring them to engage with various art materials while exploring the works of other artists alongside their own creative ideas.
The art room, based at The Hub, our newly renovated building, just across the road from the main school site, buzzes with activity not only during lessons but also hosts clubs and scholarship lessons as well as our popular Holiday Art Club. These well-resourced art and design technology facilities provide a spacious teaching area equipped with specialist tools and equipment, utilised weekly by pupils from Year 3 and upwards.
To further enhance their learning experience, pupils investigate the techniques of renowned artists and designers, visit art galleries, and partake in workshops. Our art department also offers a variety of extra-curricular clubs and maintains strong links with local designers and artists, who collaborate with us to enrich our teaching.
Pupils take great pride in displaying and exhibiting their work throughout the school and in the school magazine, which contributes to TPS’s vibrant environment. The children are encouraged to embrace the notion that everyone is a unique artist.
In Design Technology (DT), we prepare our pupils for participation in the rapidly changing world of tomorrow.
We empower them to become discerning consumers and potential innovators. Through the development of skills with a diverse range of tools and materials, pupils are encouraged to think creatively and become autonomous problem solvers. Our DT projects focus on helping pupils to identify their ideas and abilities, guiding them to create purposeful products.
Above all, our art and DT spaces offer a sanctuary for exploration and creativity, allowing pupils to unwind, express themselves, and immerse their imaginations in the joy of artistic discovery…

ISI School Inspection Report 2025
The new ISI Inspection Framework was implemented in 2023, and from this time forward schools are no longer awarded judgement ratings, such as the ‘Excellent’ which TPS achieved in all areas in 2022; instead schools are judged as to whether they have met the standards based on aspects of compliance relating to the Education Regulations 2014.
We are truly delighted that TPS has met all the required standards, reflecting our commitment to provide high-quality education and exceptional care for our pupils.
The inspection covered the following key areas:
The following extracts from the report, evidence the quality of education and provision provided by the staff at TPS, showing us to be a school where the children thrive and love to learn:
‘The School’s ethos and values are embedded across all areas.’
‘Teaching is engaging and interactive, with pupils encouraged to think independently, collaborate and participate actively in their learning.’
‘The school provides a balanced curriculum that systematically develops pupils’ skills and knowledge across a broad range of subjects.’
‘Pupils engage well with creative and physical subjects, including performances, house events and enrichment opportunities, where they demonstrate creativity, courtesy and teamwork.’
‘Leaders foster a culture where pupils feel safe, valued and respected. Positive relationships between staff and pupils contribute to a secure sense of belonging.’
‘Pupils engage in a learning environment that fosters confidence, self-esteem and self-awareness… they are motivated, demonstrating curiosity, courage and enthusiasm for learning in line with the school values.’

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Our History
Twickenham Preparatory School was founded on Twickenham Green in the Baptist Church Hall in 1969 by a group of parents, who were supposedly unhappy that the school was to be sold (with the new owner taking over from revered Headmaster, Reverend Donald Hill). So a group of parents decided to start a new school with Reverend Hill invited to be the Headmaster!
1971
From the outset, TPS was intended to be a school largely run by parents with many volunteering to help with events and creating opportunities for the children. The school moved to a permanent building opposite Twickenham Green soon afterwards, before becoming co-educational in 1971.
1992 – 1995
In 1992, with around 100 pupils enrolled, the school moved to its new home in Hampton: the ‘Beveree’, a Grade II listed building linked historically to Sir John Blow, the King’s Musician during the reign of Charles II.
The school continued to grow in size, with the addition of a purpose-built Pre-Prep building in 1995, with dedicated outdoor learning areas for every class. A new hall was built with a stage facility for productions, along with a dedicated kitchen with dining room and pupil changing facilities and cloakrooms.
2012 – 2014
In 2012, a new music and arts centre was added, named after Peter Jenkinson, a former governor and parent, along with a new amphitheatre, sports pitch and a nature trail.
2014 saw the school embark on an exciting new partnership with Kempton Cricket Club to establish the facility as the main sporting venue for girls’ and boys’ sports provision.
2020 – Today
In 2020, the school bought and renovated the Hub@51, home to a new art and design technology studio, a digital media suite and specialist classrooms for both the history and geography departments.
Today, Twickenham Prep School welcomes 260 pupils each day and is run as a charitable trust with a board of Governors, many of whom are current or past parents entrusted with continuing to build on the school’s many successes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
We recognise that pupils are more than their academic achievement and we recognise and value the children as unique individuals. In addition, we believe that our pupils have the right to learn in a happy, caring and safe environment and this includes the right to protection from all types of abuse.
That’s why Twickenham Prep School is fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of pupils and expects all staff, governors, volunteers and visitors to share this commitment.
Ensuring the health and wellbeing of our pupils and staff is integral to the work we do and we pride ourselves on taking exceptional care of our pupils mentally, physically and academically.
We are aware that safeguarding incidents could happen anywhere and staff should be alerted to possible concerns raised at the school. TPS recognises that safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility and all staff receive regular training; they remain alert for signs of any pupils in distress and are confident about applying safeguarding processes.
Any concerns about the safety or wellbeing of someone at our school should be raised with the school’s key members of staff. Please see the details below.
Designated Safeguarding Lead Mrs B Barnes (Head of Pre-Prep)
Deputy Safeguarding Leads Mr J Edwards (Deputy Head) Mrs A Hepburn (Senior Teacher)
Online Safety Co-ordinator Miss C Jones (Head of ICT & Computing)
Safeguarding Governor Mr H Warner
If you have a safeguarding concern that you would like to make the School aware of, please report it without delay to:
Email: safeguarding@twickenhamprep.co.uk
If you wish to speak with a member of the safeguarding team, please call on:
Telephone: 020 8979 6216
Key Safeguarding Contact Details Richmond Single Point of Access (SPA)
Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO)
Telephone: 020 8891 7370 /M 07774 332675
Telephone: 030 0123 1231
Email: enquiries@ofsted.gov.uk
Mental health and wellbeing
The mental health and wellbeing of the pupils, staff and parents is a key consideration at TPS, with strong focus on establishing a culture in which every member of the community is valued and recognised for their talents and achievements. For example, our weekly Celebration Assembly features children nominated for upholding the school values of being ‘Courteous’, ‘Considerate’, ‘Courageous’ and ‘Calm’, along with recognition for achievements and progress in school and beyond.
We also emphasise the importance of the development of emotional literacy and self-awareness: younger children in Pre-Prep learn about the Zones of Regulation and the older children attending BOUNCE workshops. The BOUNCE programme, run by the Raising Resilience team, is a cornerstone of the PSHE programme, teaching the children how to manage their emotions, ‘bounce back’ from disappointments and who to turn to in times of difficulty.
Our pastoral teams across the school regularly discuss children and their relationships, working closely with colleagues and visiting staff, including experts such as occupational and speech and language therapists, to ensure a collaborative and supportive approach.
Children, staff and parents all have a voice in aspects of the school’s development, resourcing and policy decisions. Our active School Council features representation from across the school, along with a vibrant House, buddy system and class partnership programme, all of which bring the community close together.
Mental health and wellbeing is overseen by the Senior Mental Health Lead, the Headmaster, Mr Oliver Barrett, along with Mental Health Champions who are part of the Mental Health Action Group.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
While the National Curriculum serves as the core of our programme here at Twickenham Prep School, we never lose sight of deeper opportunities for joyful, creative and holistic learning.
It’s all part of our unique approach which balances academic rigour with a passion for whole-child development, stretching the concept of success far beyond the classroom.
Our emphasis is in creating a thriving, happy environment through a broad curriculum, taught by dedicated and talented teachers – who nurture the children academically, socially, and emotionally.
Specialist Subject Teaching
In the early year groups, much of the teaching is delivered by class teachers supported by an assistant, ensuring that the children build strong relationships and learn to embrace school life. Along with the class teaching, we deliver specialist subject teaching from Reception onwards, including lessons in computing, French, games, library sessions, music, PE and Think Tank, a programme designed to develop strategic and tactical thinking through game play.
Dedicated Facilities
As the children move through the school, additional subject specialist teaching sessions are added, including art and design from Year 3, before all subjects are taught by specialists from Year 4 onwards. We are lucky to have purpose designed teaching spaces, including our music centre, science laboratory, sports and drama hall and art and design studio, whilst our main sports ground is located at Kempton Cricket Club.
Our pupils regularly go on visits, tours, and – for our older children – residential field trips. We also host a huge variety of events, from junior workshops to visiting speakers, specialist sports training, concerts.
Above all, our small class sizes enable staff to offer support, enrichment and challenge to suit each pupil as they explore our wonderfully rich curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We want to help busy parents – by offering a comprehensive provision of affordable wraparound care from 7:30am until 6:30pm
Early Morning Drop-Off and Breakfast Club
For those families who need to drop their children earlier in the school day, pupils are supervised in the Dining Room between 7:30am and 8am and then join Breakfast Club, which starts at 8am.
There is no charge for the 7.30am provision or for Breakfast Club if no food is eaten. Charges for food are simply added to school bills according to the register taken each day. Costs are £3.00 daily per child and on Wednesdays there is a hot breakfast choice at £4.50.
After School Care
We have an Ofsted registered after-school care provision on site, The Wrap Club. This is available for pupils in all year groups. Our pupils are offered a wide range of activities including creative projects, reading, games and sports and an opportunity to complete homework. Snacks and drinks are provided to all pupils attending. This also allows pupils to attend clubs and then go onto after-school care if needed. The provision runs daily from 4pm until 6.30pm.
For further information and to register, please contact Lisa, who manages The Wrap Club: TPSwrapclub@gmail.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Future Schools and Scholarships | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Future Schools and Scholarships
Beyond TPS: The right destination school for your child
South West London’s independent senior school sector is highly competitive and we recognise that choosing the right school for your child is an incredibly important decision.
We pride ourselves in identifying the senior schools that are best suited to our pupils, ensuring they will thrive academically and socially and have their talents and interests catered for.
Throughout your child’s time at TPS, we build up a detailed picture of their academic ability, skills, talents, character and potential. Together with our comprehensive knowledge, experience and excellent relationships with the schools that our pupils progress to, we provide valuable insight and guidance to support your decision-making.
Supported at all stages of the process
Parents can expect detailed presentations and ongoing information from Year 4 onwards; outlining sector information, senior school options, entry requirements and processes.
Our Headmaster also meets families on a one-to-one basis to provide bespoke advice tailored specifically to your child. We’re fully committed to keeping you fully informed and supported at all stages of the process.
The results for our daughter’s 11+ preparation were fantastic, but what is even more meaningful to us is how they were achieved. Throughout the process, she remained happy, confident and engaged, while being stretched just enough to reach her full potential. The balance between high achievement and her wellbeing is something we value immensely, and it speaks volumes about the care and approach taken by the school.
All pupils in Year 6 sit senior entrance exams, with offers made for Year 7 or Year 9 transfer. Where applications are for a Year 9 transition, the pupils sit the same examinations as those looking for Year 7 entry but with a deferred offer, allowing the girls and boys further time to develop as learners at TPS. Staying on at TPS Senior Prep allows the pupils to access our robust KS3 provision alongside the Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB) framework, which has a core skills focus and is designed to develop independence, leadership, creativity and collaboration.
The majority of our pupils gain places at their preferred independent day schools: popular destinations include Epsom College, Halliford, Hampton, King’s College, Kingston Grammar, Lady Eleanor Holles (LEH), Reeds, St George’s College, Sir William Perkins’s, Surbiton High, Thomas’s College and Wimbledon High, along with a number of boarding and grammar schools.
Recognising and nurturing talent is an important focus at TPS, whether it be academic, sport, art, music or drama. So we’re always delighted for our pupils when those remarkable skills and efforts are rewarded by prestigious scholarship offers from senior schools.
Above all, we’re incredibly proud of our pupils’ achievements and know that they will continue to flourish and excel as they embark on the next stage of their journey.

Starting at TPS
Reception New Joiners
Starting in Reception at Twickenham Prep School is a really exciting time for both children and their parents.
But we understand that the first day of school is a day full of emotions for everyone – so we aim to hold both your and your child’s hand through this big step!
Above all, we’re committed to ensuring a warm welcome and a smooth transition for all children regardless of their prior experience; whether they’re joining us from nursery, home or a childminder setting.
We enable Reception new joiners to start a little later on their first few days, so that they’re not overwhelmed by their new situation. Parents may accompany their child to their classroom where our friendly teaching staff will help them settle in nicely. In our experience, all Reception children are happily bouncing into school every morning within the first two weeks!
Our main focus in the first half of term is to have happy children who are keen to participate in a range of activities and new experiences in the classroom and beyond. We passionately believe that children feel secure and thrive in their learning when they are happy and settled.
Occasional Place New Joiners
If your child joins the school at a later occasional place entry point, we offer a taster day as part of the assessment process. Any child joining in September will also be invited to the summer ‘Move Up Morning’ to meet their new classmates and teachers.
Upon joining the school, new pupils are allocated a ‘buddy’ to be there for them at breaktimes or any time they need help or advice.
“As a father of a 5-year-old, I couldn’t be happier with the experience we’ve had at TPS. The school creates a warm and nurturing environment where my daughter feels safe and valued. TPS has given her the confidence and foundation she needs to succeed not just in school, but in life.”
— Year 1 Parent
Most of all, you can be reassured that we’re all deeply committed to ensuring your little one will quickly feel at home here at TPS…

pageCache.pageTitle: Join our Team | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Join our Team
At Twickenham Prep School we strive to create and maintain a positive nurturing environment with first-class facilities, excellent teaching and strong pastoral care; we recognise that our staff play a crucial role in helping to achieve this.
Working in an environment that inspires outstanding performance, we want our staff to be fully committed to high standards, ongoing professional development and supporting one other, duly focusing on the best possible outcomes for the children.
From the first day, our induction programme for new staff ensures that colleagues are made to feel welcome and supported at all times. Each member of staff is assigned a mentor to help them and there is a comprehensive training programme to ensure that colleagues are secure in their role. We have a variety of staff social events and fundraising activities which bring everyone together to build a sense of community and, most importantly, to have fun! Staff benefits include delicious school lunches, pension provision and healthcare benefits, and the leadership group are supportive and considerate in their approach.
The talent and professionalism of our staff are great strengths and visitors to the School often comment on the positive and friendly atmosphere. We have many support staff and teaching staff who have worked at TPS for many years, reflecting a long-term commitment to our values, our togetherness, and the strength of our community. We recognise that a happy, valued staff will be at their best for the children.
If you would like to join our outstanding team to help build ‘their happy place’, please get in touch to arrange a visit to meet the staff and tour our vibrant school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Facilities | Twickenham Prep School, TPS Hampton
pageCache.text:
Our Facilities
Twickenham Prep School is located in the historic Beveree building in Hampton, a leafy and affluent region of South West London close to Bushy Park, Hampton Court Palace and the River Thames.
The original building, now home to our vibrant Prep School, has been thoughtfully expanded to accommodate our growing community. It features a warm and colourful Pre-Prep, a state-of-the-art Sports and Theatre Hall, a lively dining area, and a dedicated Music Centre—all surrounded by expansive outdoor spaces, including an amphitheatre, adventure playground, and enchanting Forest School trail.
Each of our classrooms is designed to inspire, equipped with interactive electronic whiteboards that bring lessons to life, engaging both teachers and pupils. Our spacious hall is constantly buzzing with energy, hosting everything from assemblies and P.E. classes to rehearsals and lunch. The dedicated Science Lab is always alive with experiments, sparking curiosity and nurturing the next generation of scientists, while our newly renovated library offers a cosy retreat for quiet reading during lunchtime.
In 2020, we proudly opened The Hub@51, a cutting-edge facility that houses a modern Art and Design Technology studio, bright Humanities classrooms, and a high-tech digital media suite. This exciting space supports everything from film-making to photography and even hosts our school’s radio station—a pioneering feature in our local area!
Pre-Prep
Our purpose-built Pre-Prep area welcomes our youngest students in Reception through to Year 2, complete with a dedicated outdoor space for play-based learning and an ever-popular Forest School.
For Years 1 and 2, each year group has its own small garden off the classroom – which offer opportunities for hands-on learning through gardening and nature activities.
Find out more
Sports
Our site provides ample room for outdoor play and sports, supplemented by the expansive 10 acres at Kempton Cricket Club, the official home of TPS sports. Here, students engage in rugby, football, and cricket matches, as well as House events like cross-country and sports days.
Our pupils also benefit from access to the nearby Hampton Outdoor Pool, astro-turf hockey pitches, athletics tracks, and local clubs for tennis, padel and squash.
If you are interested in hiring any of our school facilities then please get in touch with the Head of Operations, Mrs Clare Shelley, email: cshelley@twickenhamprep.co.uk or call 020 8979 6216
